script: How the heck did Emiliano Martínez end up at Chelsea? Emiliano Martínez is one of the best goalkeepers on the planet, having won the World Cup with Argentina in 2022, and last season he helped Aston Villa win the Europa League. So when Chelsea announced they'd signed him this week for just 7.5 million pounds, everyone did a double take. But the reason this transfer is so shocking has nothing to do with the price, and everything to do with what happened over one specific game. See, Villa had already moved on from Dibu, because they'd spent nearly 30 million pounds on a young Japanese keeper named Zion Suzuki to be their new number one, and Martínez was left out of their squad completely. His agents needed to find him a new club fast, but meanwhile over at Chelsea, manager Xabi Alonso kept telling everyone he was happy with his goalkeepers and wasn't looking to buy anyone. But one bad 90 minutes was about to blow that plan wide open, and if you're enjoying the video, please hit the follow button. Chelsea's current keeper Robert Sánchez had a rough game against Fulham, making an error in a 3-2 win that put him under massive pressure, so Martínez's agents saw the opening and pounced, offering him straight to Chelsea within hours. The wild part is that Chelsea aren't even in Europe this season, so Dibu chose to walk away from a Champions League club for no European football at all. And that's the answer to how a World Cup winner ended up at Chelsea for pocket change.
